tasks.title: text_sha and ordinal
tasks.acceptance: text_sha is the first twelve lowercase hex characters of the sha256 of the canonical unit text, UTF-8 encoded. ordinal is the 1-based index of a unit among those sharing its hash, in emission order. §11 row 18c passes on two units with identical canonical text.
tasks.closed_reason:
- engine.FloorTextSHA (internal/engine/floor.go) is §2.1 step 5's text_sha: the first twelve lowercase hex characters of the sha256 of exactly the canonical unit string, UTF-8 encoded. - engine.FloorOrdinals is §7.2's ordinal: the 1-based index of a unit among those sharing its text_sha, in emission order, 1 when the hash is unique. It takes the HASHES rather than the units, and that is the design rather than a convenience — §7.2 keys the ordinal on text_sha and §8 joins on (text_sha, ordinal), while an implementation counting by unit text agrees on every input but a sha256 collision no test can construct, so the wrong reading would be unobservable rather than merely untested; taking the hash makes it unwriteable. Four mutants observed red: 0-based (increment after append), the global position in the round, per-hash counted from the END, and a nil return on empty input. tasks.title: the recorded row's field requirements
tasks.acceptance: §7.2's field table is a type with validation: unit_id nullable, anchor, text_sha, ordinal, verdict, kind and tier required except on NOT-A-CLAIM where they are optional, evidence required whenever tier is present, partial_kind iff PARTIAL, held_at iff partial_kind is true-when-written, causes iff QUESTION, carried_from optional. A row failing any cell is rejected naming the field.
tasks.closed_reason:

Observed red under: the forbidden branch of groundRowIff deleted (4 cells red at once); kind/tier made two-sided; evidence keyed on the verdict instead of on tier; held_at keyed on PARTIAL instead of on partial_kind; a missing unit_id read as null; a blank string read as absent; n<1 relaxed to n<0; each of the three shape patterns dropped or case-folded; an explicit null read as absent in causes and in an enum. §7.2's thirteen field names are parsed out of spec/1.0.0.md itself and matched in both directions against the fields the tests exercise, so a cell added to the spec with no case fails there — observed red by deleting one case.

A line that is not a JSON object is the one rejection that names no field, and is asserted NotErrorAs. A misspelled field literal in the implementation fails the spec-bound match, and the three shape patterns are held accountable to FloorIndexRows and FloorAnchorOf rather than to the test's own literals — observed red by changing the emitter's u<N> format, which reddens the floor round-trip test and none of the hand-written ones. Full gate green (suite-state, golangci-lint 0 issues, deadcode, complexity); tree byte-clean after every mutation.

Two claims in this code were falsified by running its own mutants and are corrected in place with the measurement beside them, because both mutants survived the whole table on the first pass. groundText's comment named {"tier": "run", "evidence": ""} as the row a blank-reads-as-absent parser would let through: that row is rejected either way and names the same field, because a blank on a REQUIRED cell simply becomes a missing cell. The rows that do separate the two readings are ones whose condition does not hold — a blank evidence with no tier, a blank held_at on a two-readings row — and both are now cases. groundCauses' comment made the identical error about null on a QUESTION row; the row that separates them is a non-QUESTION row carrying "causes": null, which is what a Go emitter writes by accident since a nil slice marshals to null.

Behaviourally: §11 row 4's own named input (a unit holding the non-hex token zqxjvwkfgb, searched for in the index) plus an exhaustive grammar `^(?:u\d+ §[0-9.]+ [0-9a-f]{12} #\d+ \d+B\n)+$` that accounts for every byte of the index, leaving nowhere for text to sit.
- §11 row 4 passes on a constructed 1,200-unit floor at the worst case §2.2 admits, and the floor is derived from text rather than hand-built structs so the row's named mutant fails the size half too: 1,200 identical 1,045-byte units (ordinal reaches 1200, four digits; length field four digits; id u1200) under a seven-segment anchor §1.2.3.4.5.6.7 — each of those three properties asserted, since each is what makes the case a worst case. Index 56,400 bytes against the bound of 1200*48+256 = 57,856. The named mutant (carry the first 60 bytes of each unit) was built and run: 127,386 bytes, 2.2x the bound, and it failed all three assertions of the row including the token search and the grammar.
- The port was cross-checked against scripts/floor-prototype.py rather than trusted: a throwaway probe emitted (unit_id, text_sha, ordinal, byte length) for every floor unit of all 54 spec/*.md and diffed byte-for-byte against the prototype's --emit rows — 5,311 rows, zero disagreements, on ids that count cut units. The probe is deleted and the tree is byte-clean. The same corpus under this encoding is 159,334 bytes against a bound of 255,184, mean 30 bytes per row.
- Out of scope: (1) §2.2 says the anchor is emitted in "the labelled shape internal/cli/review.go:1054 already uses", but that line renders "Table '%s' (line %d, %d rows)" — word labels — while the encoding the spec's own byte figures were measured from is scripts/floor-prototype.py's sigil form `u1 §7.2 <sha> #1 21B`. The citation does not describe the encoding that was measured; the sigil form is what is ported, because it is the one the bound was derived against. (2) The anchor is a parameter (anchorOf) rather than derived here, since §7.3's rule needs the unit's line in the file and anchor-zero owns it; but cmd-emit's depends_on does not include anchor-zero, so on the current graph the emit task can be reached with no anchor derivation in the tree.

tasks.title: cut rows, the commit line and the summary
tasks.acceptance: A cut unit emits its id and anchor with no hash and no text. The first line names the commit the index was derived from. The summary counts units rather than distinct hashes.
source_sections: ### 2.2 The floor is a coverage obligation, not a shortlist
tasks.closed_reason:
- A cut unit now emits its id and anchor and nothing else: FloorIndexRows (internal/engine/floor.go) returns a row for EVERY unit §2.1 produces and FloorIndexRow.String renders `u2 §2 (cut)` for one carrying no hash. There is no Cut flag — the ABSENCE of the hash is the cut, so a row marked cut that still ships a hash is unwriteable, and that reading is sound because FloorTextSHA returns twelve hex characters for every input including "" (required in the test, not assumed). Two mutants observed red on TestACutUnitEmitsItsIdAndAnchorWithNoHashAndNoText, whose cut unit sits BETWEEN two floor units — the only arrangement in which the row can be seen to occupy an id: HEAD's floor-only rows (2 rows, not 3) and String with the cut branch deleted (`u2 §2  #0 0B`).
- The first line names the commit: FormatFloorIndex(commit, rows) writes `# commit <sha>` ahead of the rows, and `# commit unknown` when the caller has none, so the line is unconditional and `unknown` cannot be read as a revision. TestTheIndexNamesTheCommitOnItsFirstLine holds three assertions proven not to subsume each other by running each mutant: the parameter accepted and dropped and the line moved below the rows each leave line 1 reading `u1 §1 ...`; a hard-coded `7ced1edb` fails ONLY the second commit's assertion; omitting the line on an empty commit fails ONLY the `unknown` one, with the other two green.
- The summary counts units, not distinct hashes: the last line is `# <floor> in floor, <cut> cut`, counted over the rows. TestTheSummaryCountsUnitsNotDistinctHashes uses the one arrangement where the readings differ — two floor units of identical canonical text plus a cut one, with "2 units, 1 distinct hash" required rather than assumed — and both named mutants were observed red there while the cut, commit and row-4 cases stayed green: counting distinct hashes gives `# 1 in floor, 1 cut`, counting every row as floor gives `# 3 in floor, 0 cut`.
- Dogfooded against the release's own spec through a throwaway probe (deleted): the Go index over spec/1.0.0.md agrees with `python3 scripts/floor-prototype.py --emit spec/1.0.0.md` unit for unit — same first rows, 367 unit rows, `# 274 in floor, 93 cut` in both. §11 row 4's exhaustive grammar was extended to cover the whole artifact (commit line, cut rows, summary), so it still accounts for every byte and leaves nowhere for unit text to sit.
- Gate green at the closing commit: check-suite-state, golangci-lint (0 issues), check-deadcode, check-complexity all exit 0.
Out of scope: §2.2 states the cut row and the commit line but says NOTHING about a summary line — the acceptance criterion's wording and the counting rule come from scripts/floor-prototype.py, and `# commit unknown` for a caller with no commit is a decision this task made rather than one the spec settles; both are recorded in the doc comments. The prototype's summary also reports how many table data rows were segmented into units; that clause is deliberately not ported, because it is derived from the spec's text and FormatFloorIndex takes rows precisely so the text is out of its reach. Also recorded: making every unit a row cost the previous task's "anchorOf is called with the unit's id, not the row's index" assertion its discriminating power (with a row per unit the two numbers are identical, so no input separates them); the distinction survives in FloorUnitRows, and the comment in floor_test.go says so rather than leaving a green assertion that proves nothing.

tasks.title: tp ground --units prints the floor units with their text
tasks.acceptance: tp ground <spec> --units prints one line per floor unit carrying the whole canonical unit text and the same text_sha the index row for that unit carries, in emission order (§11 row 4b). The flag is added to the command-surface baseline in internal/cli. engine.FloorUnitRows and engine.FormatFloorUnits gain a production caller: before this task they are reachable only from tests, which is the test-only sink CLAUDE.md names.
tasks.closed_reason:
- `tp ground <spec> --units` (internal/cli/ground.go, runGroundUnits) prints one line per floor unit, `<unit_id>\t<text_sha>\t<text>`, in emission order: it reads the spec named on the command line, takes no lock and writes nothing. Dogfooded on a copy of spec/1.0.0.md outside the repository — 318 lines against the emitted index's 318 floor rows, ids equal to the index's order, every line's sha equal to that index row's sha AND to the sha256 of the text on the line, every line's UTF-8 length equal to that row's Bytes; 289 of the 318 units exceed 60 bytes, so §11 row 4b's named truncation mutant would be visible on 91% of the document.
- The WHOLE-unit and same-hash claims are pinned against the EMITTED index read back from disk, not against one re-derived in the test (TestGroundUnitsPrintsEveryFloorUnitWholeWithTheIndexsHash). Row 4b's own mutant — truncate to 60 bytes — observed red on the index-hash equality and on the byte-length equality. Its second clause, "the text_sha on that line is the sha256 of what follows it", stayed GREEN under that mutant and cannot be made to fail: FloorUnitRow has no settable hash field, so the hash is derived from whatever text is printed. The length read from the index is what catches a truncation; row 4b's second clause is unwriteable-false rather than tested.
- The flag is on the command-surface baseline (`ground: check record status units` in internal/cli/nongoals_surface_test.go) and in SKILL.md's flag inventory; TestNonGoals_NoCommandOrFlagIsAdded and TestSkillFlagInventoryIsComplete both green. engine.FloorUnitRows and engine.FormatFloorUnits now have their production caller — TestGroundUnitsReadsTheSpecAndWritesNothing asserts stdout equals FormatFloorUnits(FloorUnitRows(fixture)) byte for byte, and a mutant returning an output.JSON envelope under the piped convention was observed red there and on the line-shape require (the envelope also drops text_sha entirely, since FloorUnitRow has no such field).
- Five more mutants observed red, each on the assertion written for it: floor-alone numbering (ids u1,u2 for u1,u4 — the index's u2 is a CUT row with 0 bytes, so the join breaks); an emission written before the print (red on the state-directory assertion ALONE, stdout being identical, which is why that assertion exists); the mode fence reverted to the shipped two-flag form (both subtests of TestGroundUnitsIsAModeOfItsOwn red at exit 0 — the mode the operator did not ask for); and, wide, an engine FloorUnitRows emitting cut units too (red here on the line count and on two engine guards). No mutant survived.
- Mutation found a defect in my own test and it is fixed in d89506c3: the `require.Greater(…, 60)` fixture fact was computed from stdout, so the truncation mutant falsified the require's own message ("the fixture must hold a unit longer than a sixty-byte head" — the fixture did; the output did not). It now reads the length off the emitted index, and under the same mutant it stays green while the two assertions written for that mutant fail.
- §7.1's mode table pairs no two flags, so `--units` joins the existing refusal: groundModesPassed counts the three mode-selecting flags and refuses any pairing before any of them opens a file, which is why `--units --record <missing>` is exit 2 (usage) and not exit 3. Registering the flag without this would have let the dispatch's order resolve the pair — the defect the shipped comment already names.
- Quality gate green in four separate runs: check-suite-state 0, golangci-lint 0 issues, check-deadcode 0, check-complexity 0.

Out of scope: §7.1 and §11 row 4b never say WHICH text `--units` reads, and the plain reading of `tp ground <spec> --units` — implemented here — is the spec named on the command line. That is the only reading under which row 4b is testable at all (reading a round's frozen snapshot would exit 3 on a spec with no emission), but it means that after an edit between emit and record the listing disagrees with the frozen index the prompt carries — precisely the divergence §7.3 freezes the snapshot to prevent for `--record`. The spec states the no-re-derivation rule for `--record` only. A later release may want `--units` to prefer the latest emitted snapshot when one exists.

tasks.title: The emitted prompt asks only for the dispositions a round owes
tasks.acceptance: An emission whose preceding round dispositioned units that still carry marks each carrying unit in the index and asks for dispositions only for the rest, while the index still lists every unit (§2.2). §11 row 16b passes: on a spec whose round 1 dispositioned every unit and whose round 2 changes one unit text, the round-2 prompt asks for one disposition. The carry set is computed by the same engine.groundCarryForward join that --record uses, never by a second rule.
